title: Software Requirements Specification + Requirements Traceability Matrix — DK Bond Tracker

sections.heading: Purpose and Scope
sections.body:
This document is the Software Requirements Specification (SRS) and Requirements Traceability Matrix (RTM) for the DK Bond Tracker rebuild: replacing the macro-enabled workbook `v5.5_40L_Project_Tracker.xlsm` with a local SQLite database plus a Flask web UI. It carries every requirement from `docs/PRD_DK_Bond_Tracker_v2.json` forward one-to-one (FR-01..FR-24, NFR-1..NFR-13, DATA-01..DATA-05 — 42 entries), each with a verification method and Given/When/Then acceptance criteria, and it carries the legacy VBA RTM mapping (`docs/RTM.json`) forward into the `rtm` section so no legacy behavior row is dropped.

**In scope:** local per-user SQLite schema (bond master, payment ledger, home plan), Flask server-rendered UI with Excel-like month grid, one-time XLSM import (Excel stays read-only backup), live dashboard queries, the fixed status engine (decision D5), CSV export, quirk fixes (visible errors, no hardcoded month windows, always-live dashboard), and later-phase features (watch-list analytics, Home Plan schedule, discount/TDS/payout cycles, P&L).

**Out of scope:** cloud sync, accounts/authentication, mobile apps, networked multi-user mode, live market data, and any modification of the source XLSM file. Actors: the owner (primary), friends running a copied folder on their own machines (secondary), and spreadsheet/CSV consumers (tertiary, read-only outside the system).

sections.heading: Definitions
sections.body:
**Bond** — a fixed-income investment record held in the bond master table: ISN, company, rating, principal TL amount, tenure in months, maturity date/amount, purchase date, broker, interest start and payment type.

**Bond status** — one of Danger / On-going / Completed computed by the status engine from the payment ledger; never stored as a static value.

**Danger** — status meaning at least one past-month payment is unpaid (D5 rule: ANY unpaid past month, not only the previous month).

**Completed** — status meaning the bond has paid for its full tenure (months paid >= tenure); Completed overrides Danger.

**On-going** — status for a bond with no unpaid past month that has not yet reached full tenure.

**Zero = unpaid** — a payment row with amount 0 counts as unpaid for every status calculation (D5).

**Ledger / payment ledger** — one row per payment (bond ref, month, amount, paid flag); the single payment storage model (D3). All totals, statuses and grids are derived from it by live queries.

**Month grid** — the Excel-like view with months across columns, rendered from ledger rows (not stored columns).

**Till Return** — sum of paid ledger rows for a bond (legacy Excel column K); query-only, never stored.

**Balance** — Till Return minus Maturity Amount (legacy Excel column L); negative means still to receive; query-only.

**Home Plan** — the 84-month savings simulation schedule (month index 1..84, irregular savings such as 25000, 10000, 0, rate, per-year interest, countdown, remaining interest, totals).

**Watch list** — the static analytics view reproducing discount, TDS, per-month, qty TL and 12-month formulas per bond.

**ISN** — the bond identifier column from the workbook (legacy header spelling retained only as a display label; schema key is stable, per FR-23).

sections.heading: Overview of the Flask Local App
sections.body:
The system is a single local folder a friend can copy to any desktop machine: a Python project with Flask, SQLite and the project venv (`.venv`, Python 3.14). One documented launch command starts a Flask server bound to localhost, and a browser opens the server-rendered HTML UI — no build step, no npm, no bundler (FR-02, D1).

The UI has three main surfaces: (1) the **month grid** — an Excel-like sheet with months across, rendered from payment ledger rows, cells colored green (paid) / light red (due) and status cells red/orange/green (FR-04); (2) the **live dashboard** — portfolio summary counts and amounts, this-month returns, full monthly history and the bonds status overview, every figure computed as a query/view on each request (FR-05, FR-20, NFR-7); (3) **detail/plan views** — bond detail, Home Plan and watch list, plus CSV export of any displayed dataset (FR-07, NFR-12).

Data lives in exactly one local SQLite file per user (D10, NFR-2, NFR-13) — sharing is folder copy plus DB file copy, never a server. The one-time import script (FR-08, D2) reads the original XLSM once and populates SQLite; the Excel file remains a read-only backup that the tool never writes. Business logic is centralized in one module plus SQL views (NFR-5); failures surface visibly in the UI instead of being swallowed (FR-21, NFR-6). The app works fully offline (NFR-1) and reaches a working dashboard on a clean machine within 1 minute via one command (NFR-4).

sections.heading: Data Model Summary
sections.body:
Three persisted tables in one SQLite file, matching DATA-01..DATA-05 and decision D3 (row-per-payment ledger; totals/status become live queries):

1. **bonds (bond master, DATA-01)** — one row per bond: status reference, purchase date, broker, ISN, company name, rating, principle TL amount, tenure (months), maturity date, maturity amount, interest start, payment type. 15 rows after importing the real workbook (FR-10).
2. **payment_ledger (DATA-02)** — one row per payment: bond ref, month (Sep-2025..Jul-2032+), amount, paid flag. No month columns ever exist in the schema (FR-01, FR-03); the month grid is rendered from these rows (FR-04).
3. **home_plan (DATA-03)** — one row per schedule month: month index 1..84, saving amount (incl. irregular values 25000, 10000, 0), rate, per-year interest, countdown, remaining interest, plus schedule totals; stored values preserved verbatim on import (FR-12, ERR-06).

**Query-only derived data (DATA-05):** Till Return, Balance and status are computed by SQL views/functions at read time and are never stored as columns. Watch-list analytics fields (DATA-04: face value, principle, T.L.P, discount, per-month, 10% TDS, 12-month, qty, TL principle) are computed on view for FR-11. The month window (grid columns, status scan range) is derived from bond start month + tenure — no hardcoded headers (Sep-2025..Feb-2027) and no scan-window limit (FR-18, FR-19, NFR-9).

sections.heading: Status Engine Rules (D5)
sections.body:
The status engine replaces the old VBA single-month check. Decision **D5** (CONFIRMED) states the fixed rules verbatim: **Danger = ANY unpaid past month (not just previous month); Completed overrides Danger when months paid >= tenure; zero-value = unpaid preserved.**

Operational reading used by FR-06, FR-19, FR-24 and NFR-8:

1. Evaluate every past month in the bond's due window (start month .. min(current month, start+tenure-1)). If ANY of those months is unpaid — no row, paid flag false, or amount 0 — the status is **Danger**, even when the immediately previous month is paid.
2. If months paid >= tenure, the status is **Completed**, and Completed **overrides** Danger (a completed bond with an old miss still reads Completed).
3. Otherwise the status is **On-going**.
4. A zero-value payment row counts as unpaid everywhere the rules scan (ERR-02).
5. There is no scan-window limit: a bond whose window starts Feb-2031 or later is evaluated by the same rules and still gets status + grid (FR-19, ERR-01).
6. Status is recomputed from the ledger on every view — never stored, never waiting for an open/save event (FR-24, NFR-7).

sections.heading: Verification Methods
sections.body: Check methods used in `requirements[].check_method`: **unit** — automated test of one function/query (e.g. computeBondStatus) against fixture data; **integration** — automated test across import/storage/query layers (e.g. import reconciliation); **manual review** — a human runs the described scenario in the UI and compares against the acceptance criteria; **gate** — pass/fail threshold that blocks progression (performance, clean-machine launch, error-surfacing); **inspection** — reading code/query definitions or comparing output values side by side (e.g. code review of schema-key access, formula comparison vs Excel). Acceptance criteria are Given/When/Then statements; test bindings for them are added at Stage 8 (test_plan) per the derivation rule in the `rtm` section.

requirements.text: The system SHALL store all data in a local SQLite database schema comprising a bond master table, a row-per-payment ledger table (one row per payment: bond ref, month, amount, paid flag — the D3 model where totals and statuses become live queries over the ledger), and a home_plan table.

acceptance_criteria.given: a fresh project folder with no database file
acceptance_criteria.when: the application initializes or the import script runs
acceptance_criteria.then: a SQLite file is created containing tables bonds, payment_ledger and home_plan with their documented columns

acceptance_criteria.given: the schema of the created database
acceptance_criteria.when: it is inspected for month storage
acceptance_criteria.then: no per-month columns exist anywhere — payment months are represented only as rows in payment_ledger

requirements.text: When a user starts the application, the system SHALL serve a Flask web UI locally as server-rendered HTML with no build step, requiring only Python and a browser.

acceptance_criteria.given: a clean machine with only Python, the project folder and a browser
acceptance_criteria.when: the user runs the single documented launch command
acceptance_criteria.then: a local Flask server starts and the dashboard loads in the browser as plain server-rendered HTML with no npm or bundler step

requirements.text: When a payment is recorded, the system SHALL store it as exactly one payment_ledger row (bond ref, month, amount, paid flag) instead of a month column.

acceptance_criteria.given: an imported bond with no payment for Sep-2025
acceptance_criteria.when: the user records a payment of 10000 for Sep-2025
acceptance_criteria.then: payment_ledger gains exactly one new row with that bond ref, month 2025-09, amount 10000 and paid flag set

acceptance_criteria.given: the same recorded payment
acceptance_criteria.when: the table structure is inspected
acceptance_criteria.then: no schema change occurred — no column was added to any table

requirements.text: When the user opens the month grid, the system SHALL render an Excel-like grid (months across) derived from ledger rows, coloring paid cells green, due cells light red, and status cells red/orange/green for Danger/On-going/Completed.

acceptance_criteria.given: a bond with one paid month and one unpaid past month in its ledger
acceptance_criteria.when: the month grid renders
acceptance_criteria.then: the paid month cell is green and the unpaid due month cell is light red

acceptance_criteria.given: bonds with statuses Danger, On-going and Completed
acceptance_criteria.when: the grid renders their status cells
acceptance_criteria.then: the cells are colored red, orange and green respectively

requirements.text: When the user views the dashboard, the system SHALL compute all figures (portfolio summary counts/amounts, this-month returns, monthly history, status overview) as live queries/views over the current ledger and bond data.

acceptance_criteria.given: a dashboard rendered once from current data
acceptance_criteria.when: a payment is added and the dashboard is requested again
acceptance_criteria.then: every figure (counts, totals, this-month returns, history, status overview) equals the query result over the updated data

acceptance_criteria.given: the dashboard response payload
acceptance_criteria.when: it is checked for cached values
acceptance_criteria.then: no figure comes from a stored snapshot table — each is produced by a query or view at request time

requirements.text: The status engine SHALL apply decision D5 exactly: Danger = ANY unpaid past month (not just previous month); Completed overrides Danger when months paid >= tenure; zero-value = unpaid preserved — so any missing or zero past-month payment yields Danger, full tenure yields Completed regardless of earlier misses, and a zero-amount row counts as unpaid.

acceptance_criteria.given: a 12-month bond whose month 3 is unpaid while every later past month including the previous month is paid
acceptance_criteria.when: the status engine computes the status
acceptance_criteria.then: the status is Danger because ANY unpaid past month triggers Danger

acceptance_criteria.given: a bond with months paid >= tenure that previously had an unpaid month
acceptance_criteria.when: the status engine computes the status
acceptance_criteria.then: the status is Completed, overriding Danger

acceptance_criteria.given: a past month whose ledger row exists with amount 0
acceptance_criteria.when: the status engine evaluates that month
acceptance_criteria.then: the month counts as unpaid and contributes to Danger

requirements.text: When the user requests an export, the system SHALL produce a UTF-8 CSV of any displayed dataset, replacing any xlsx export.

acceptance_criteria.given: any dataset currently displayed (dashboard table, grid, Home Plan)
acceptance_criteria.when: the user clicks export
acceptance_criteria.then: a UTF-8 CSV file downloads whose rows and headers match the displayed data

acceptance_criteria.given: the downloaded CSV containing rupee amounts
acceptance_criteria.when: it is opened in a spreadsheet application
acceptance_criteria.then: it parses into the correct columns with no encoding errors

requirements.text: When the import script is run, the system SHALL read the source XLSM once and populate SQLite, keeping the Excel file as a read-only backup that is never modified.

acceptance_criteria.given: the original v5.5_40L_Project_Tracker.xlsm with a recorded SHA-256 hash
acceptance_criteria.when: the import script completes
acceptance_criteria.then: SQLite holds the parsed data and the XLSM file's hash and modification time are unchanged

acceptance_criteria.given: a corrupt or unreadable XLSM file
acceptance_criteria.when: the import script runs
acceptance_criteria.then: the failure is reported explicitly (ERR-05) and no partial silent import is presented as success

requirements.text: When payments exist, the system SHALL compute Till Return as the sum of paid ledger rows and Balance as Till Return minus Maturity Amount, as queries only — these totals are never stored (DATA-05).

acceptance_criteria.given: a bond with paid ledger rows totalling 30000 and a maturity amount of 120000
acceptance_criteria.when: the total queries run
acceptance_criteria.then: Till Return equals 30000 and Balance equals -90000

acceptance_criteria.given: the database schema after any query execution
acceptance_criteria.when: the bonds table is inspected
acceptance_criteria.then: no persisted Till Return or Balance column exists

requirements.text: When import completes, the system SHALL hold all 15 bonds' master fields exactly as in the source workbook (ISN, company, rating, principle TL, tenure, maturity date/amount, purchase date, broker, interest start, payment type).

acceptance_criteria.given: the real source workbook with 15 bonds
acceptance_criteria.when: the import completes
acceptance_criteria.then: the bonds table contains exactly 15 rows

acceptance_criteria.given: the imported 15 rows and the workbook values
acceptance_criteria.when: a field-by-field comparison is made
acceptance_criteria.then: every master field of every bond matches the source value

requirements.text: When the watch list is viewed, the system SHALL reproduce the analytics formulas (discount, TDS, per-month, qty TL, 12-month totals) over the imported watch-list fields (DATA-04).

acceptance_criteria.given: imported watch-list rows for a bond (face value, principle, T.L.P, discount inputs)
acceptance_criteria.when: the watch list view is rendered
acceptance_criteria.then: computed discount, 10% TDS, per-month, qty TL and 12-month totals match the Excel watch-list outputs for the same bond

requirements.text: When the Home Plan is viewed, the system SHALL reproduce the 84-month savings schedule including the irregular savings values 25000, 10000 and 0, with rate, per-year interest, countdown, remaining interest and totals preserved from stored Excel values.

acceptance_criteria.given: imported home_plan rows for months 1..84
acceptance_criteria.when: the Home Plan view renders
acceptance_criteria.then: all 84 months are listed and the irregular savings 25000, 10000 and 0 appear in their original month positions

acceptance_criteria.given: the rendered schedule and the stored Excel values
acceptance_criteria.when: rate, per-year interest, countdown, remaining interest and totals are compared row by row
acceptance_criteria.then: every value matches the stored Excel value (ERR-06: formula/static mix preserved verbatim)

requirements.text: When a bond has a discount, the system SHALL record and display the discount amount per bond.

acceptance_criteria.given: a bond recorded with a purchase discount
acceptance_criteria.when: the bond detail view opens
acceptance_criteria.then: the discount amount for that bond is displayed alongside its other master fields

requirements.text: When a payout is due, the system SHALL compute and display the TDS deduction on that payout.

acceptance_criteria.given: a due payout of 10000 on a bond subject to 10% TDS
acceptance_criteria.when: the payout is computed
acceptance_criteria.then: TDS of 1000 is shown with the payout alongside the net amount of 9000

requirements.text: When a bond's payment type is quarterly or yearly, the system SHALL generate due dates on that cycle instead of monthly.

acceptance_criteria.given: a bond with payment type quarterly whose interest starts Sep-2025 and a 24-month tenure
acceptance_criteria.when: the due schedule is generated
acceptance_criteria.then: due dates fall on Sep-2025, Dec-2025, Mar-2026 and so on through the tenure, not on every month

acceptance_criteria.given: a bond with payment type yearly
acceptance_criteria.when: the due schedule is generated
acceptance_criteria.then: exactly one due date falls in each year of the tenure

requirements.text: When the dashboard is viewed, the system SHALL show P&L and the ongoing bond total (TL) value computed from current data.

acceptance_criteria.given: a portfolio containing completed and on-going bonds
acceptance_criteria.when: the dashboard is viewed
acceptance_criteria.then: a P&L figure and an ongoing TL value are both displayed

acceptance_criteria.given: the displayed P&L and ongoing TL figures
acceptance_criteria.when: they are recomputed with the dashboard queries
acceptance_criteria.then: both match the query results over current ledger and bond data

requirements.text: When a bond reaches Completed, the system SHALL free its principal for reinvestment, and duplicate-deduction rules SHALL apply only to On-going and Danger bonds — a Completed bond's principal is never deducted twice.

acceptance_criteria.given: a bond with status Completed and principal 100000
acceptance_criteria.when: the reinvestment free-up figure is computed
acceptance_criteria.then: 100000 is reported as available principal to reinvest

acceptance_criteria.given: a mix of Completed, On-going and Danger bonds
acceptance_criteria.when: duplicate-deduction rules run
acceptance_criteria.then: deductions apply only to the On-going and Danger bonds and the Completed bond is excluded from deduction

requirements.text: When the current month is beyond a fixed range, the system SHALL still generate grid columns/borders dynamically from the derived month window with no hardcoded Feb-2027 header limit and no schema change.

acceptance_criteria.given: a simulated current month of Aug-2027, beyond the old hardcoded header window ending Feb-2027
acceptance_criteria.when: the month grid renders
acceptance_criteria.then: columns are generated continuously through the current month with correct borders and no missing months

acceptance_criteria.given: the database schema before and after rendering the extended grid
acceptance_criteria.when: both are compared
acceptance_criteria.then: the schema is unchanged — columns are derived at render time

requirements.text: When a bond's payment window starts Feb-2031 or later, the system SHALL still compute status under decision D5 (Danger = ANY unpaid past month (not just previous month); Completed overrides Danger when months paid >= tenure; zero-value = unpaid preserved) and render its rows — there is no scan-window limit.

acceptance_criteria.given: a seeded bond whose payment window starts Feb-2031 with a 60-month tenure
acceptance_criteria.when: the status engine computes its status
acceptance_criteria.then: a status is produced by the D5 rules instead of being skipped or left blank

acceptance_criteria.given: the same Feb-2031 bond with one unpaid past month
acceptance_criteria.when: the month grid renders
acceptance_criteria.then: all of its month rows render with correct coloring and no month is dropped by any window limit (ERR-01)

requirements.text: When data changes, the system SHALL refresh the dashboard on the next view without requiring any open/save event trigger.

acceptance_criteria.given: an open dashboard showing current totals
acceptance_criteria.when: the user records a new payment elsewhere in the app
acceptance_criteria.then: reloading the dashboard view shows the updated figures with no file open, save or restart performed

requirements.text: When an operation fails, the system SHALL surface the error to the user visibly and SHALL NOT swallow errors silently.

acceptance_criteria.given: an induced failure such as an unreadable XLSM file during import
acceptance_criteria.when: the operation runs
acceptance_criteria.then: an explicit error message is shown to the user naming the failed operation

acceptance_criteria.given: the same induced failure
acceptance_criteria.when: the app state afterwards is inspected
acceptance_criteria.then: no silent fallback (default zeros, empty success) is presented as a completed operation

requirements.text: When a duplicate ISN exists in the bond set, the system SHALL flag it across the entire set, not only within a partial row range.

acceptance_criteria.given: a bond set where the same ISN appears on row 2 and on row 40 of 40 bonds
acceptance_criteria.when: duplicate validation runs
acceptance_criteria.then: both occurrences are flagged (ERR-04)

requirements.text: When data is read or written, the system SHALL use stable schema keys and SHALL NOT couple logic to header text or column positions.

acceptance_criteria.given: code that reads bond or ledger fields
acceptance_criteria.when: it is reviewed
acceptance_criteria.then: field access uses stable schema keys, never matching on workbook header strings or hard-coded column numbers

acceptance_criteria.given: a renamed display label such as correcting Staus to Status
acceptance_criteria.when: the UI label is changed
acceptance_criteria.then: no query, status rule or import logic changes behavior as a result

requirements.text: When payment history changes, the system SHALL recompute the bond status immediately under decision D5 rules (Danger = ANY unpaid past month (not just previous month); Completed overrides Danger when months paid >= tenure; zero-value = unpaid preserved) without requiring any open/save event.

acceptance_criteria.given: a bond currently On-going with all past months paid
acceptance_criteria.when: an older past-month payment is removed or set to 0
acceptance_criteria.then: the next status read returns Danger

acceptance_criteria.given: a Completed bond
acceptance_criteria.when: payment history changes and status is recomputed
acceptance_criteria.then: the status stays Completed because Completed overrides Danger when months paid >= tenure

acceptance_criteria.given: the recomputed status
acceptance_criteria.when: no file open/save/restart event occurs
acceptance_criteria.then: the new status is already visible on the next view

requirements.text: The system SHALL operate entirely offline for all features — no feature may require network access.

acceptance_criteria.given: a machine with network connectivity disabled
acceptance_criteria.when: the full workflow runs: launch, import, record payment, view dashboard, export CSV
acceptance_criteria.then: every step completes successfully with no network-dependent error

requirements.text: The system SHALL keep all data in a local SQLite file with no cloud service, no accounts and no outbound data transmission.

acceptance_criteria.given: the application running through its full workflow
acceptance_criteria.when: network traffic and configuration are inspected
acceptance_criteria.then: no outbound connection is made and no credential or account mechanism exists in the code or config

acceptance_criteria.given: the project folder
acceptance_criteria.when: the persistence layer is inspected
acceptance_criteria.then: all application data resides in a single local SQLite database file

requirements.text: The system SHALL run on any desktop OS with only Python and a browser, with no build step.

acceptance_criteria.given: Windows, Linux and macOS desktops each with Python and a browser
acceptance_criteria.when: the documented launch command runs on each
acceptance_criteria.then: the dashboard loads and all core features work on every OS without any build tooling

requirements.text: When launched on a clean machine, the system SHALL reach a working dashboard within 1 minute via a single documented command.

acceptance_criteria.given: a clean machine with only Python and the copied project folder
acceptance_criteria.when: the single documented launch command is run and timed
acceptance_criteria.then: a working dashboard displaying live data is visible in the browser within 60 seconds

requirements.text: The system SHALL centralize business logic in one module and SQL views and SHALL NOT recreate Excel's header-text coupling.

acceptance_criteria.given: the application source tree
acceptance_criteria.when: code review looks for duplicated status/totals logic and header-string matching
acceptance_criteria.then: status and totals logic exists in one place backed by SQL views, with no logic keyed on header text

requirements.text: The system SHALL surface errors visibly to the user and SHALL NOT swallow failures silently.

acceptance_criteria.given: induced failures for import, export and view rendering
acceptance_criteria.when: each operation runs
acceptance_criteria.then: each failure produces a visible message and none is suppressed by an ignore-and-continue handler

requirements.text: When a view is requested, the system SHALL recompute dashboard and status values from current data and SHALL NOT serve stale snapshots.

acceptance_criteria.given: a dashboard rendered at time T
acceptance_criteria.when: a payment is recorded at time T+1 and the dashboard is requested at time T+2
acceptance_criteria.then: the response reflects the T+1 payment with no open/save event

acceptance_criteria.given: two consecutive view requests with no data change
acceptance_criteria.when: the responses are compared
acceptance_criteria.then: both are computed fresh by queries and are identical

requirements.text: The system SHALL enforce the D5 data-integrity rules everywhere status is computed: Danger = any past unpaid month; Completed overrides Danger when months paid >= tenure; zero-value = unpaid (verification obligation for FR-06).

acceptance_criteria.given: a fixture portfolio with seeded gaps in different months, a zero-amount payment and a fully paid bond
acceptance_criteria.when: the status engine runs over the fixture
acceptance_criteria.then: every bond's status matches the expected D5 outcome: any past gap yields Danger, the fully paid bond yields Completed, and the zero amount counts as unpaid

requirements.text: The system SHALL NOT use hardcoded date headers or scan-window limits; month windows SHALL be derived at runtime.

acceptance_criteria.given: boundary cases with the current month in Feb-2027 or later and a bond starting Feb-2031 or later
acceptance_criteria.when: the month window and status scan run
acceptance_criteria.then: all months are produced correctly with no hardcoded header list or Jan-2031 cutoff clipping the result

acceptance_criteria.given: the source code
acceptance_criteria.when: it is searched for literal month header strings
acceptance_criteria.then: no hardcoded Sep-2025..Feb-2027 header sequence or fixed scan end date exists

requirements.text: When import runs, the system SHALL reproduce the full dataset with totals reconciling exactly: 15 bonds, Total Investment 550000.00, Total Till Return 28500.00, Total Balance -521500.00.

acceptance_criteria.given: the real source XLSM
acceptance_criteria.when: the import completes and reconciliation queries run
acceptance_criteria.then: bond count is 15, Total Investment is 550000.00, Total Till Return is 28500.00 and Total Balance is -521500.00, all exactly equal to the Excel-derived figures

requirements.text: The system SHALL render the dashboard in under 2 seconds with 150 bonds x 96 months of data without any schema change.

acceptance_criteria.given: a seeded database with 150 bonds and 96 months of ledger rows
acceptance_criteria.when: the dashboard view is requested and timed
acceptance_criteria.then: the response completes in under 2 seconds with the schema unchanged from the 15-bond layout

requirements.text: The system SHALL provide CSV export of any displayed dataset.

acceptance_criteria.given: each data-displaying view in the app (dashboard tables, month grid, Home Plan, watch list, bond detail)
acceptance_criteria.when: its export is triggered
acceptance_criteria.then: a CSV containing that view's rows and headers is produced for every view

requirements.text: The system SHALL keep the database file as the sole persistence artifact, transferable to another machine by plain file copy.

acceptance_criteria.given: machine A with a populated SQLite DB file
acceptance_criteria.when: the DB file (with the app folder) is copied to machine B and opened there
acceptance_criteria.then: machine B shows the same bonds, payments and dashboard figures with no additional migration or server step

acceptance_criteria.given: the app folder on machine A
acceptance_criteria.when: other persistence locations (external service, second database, cache file) are searched
acceptance_criteria.then: none exist — the single DB file holds all state

requirements.text: The system SHALL persist a bond master entity (DATA-01) with the fields status reference, purchase date, broker, ISN, company, rating, principle TL, tenure, maturity date/amount, interest start and payment type, backing FR-10.

acceptance_criteria.given: an imported bond
acceptance_criteria.when: the bonds table row is read back
acceptance_criteria.then: every listed field is present and holds the value imported from the workbook

requirements.text: The system SHALL persist a payment ledger entity (DATA-02) with bond ref, month and paid flag (amount included per FR-03) covering Sep-2025..Jul-2032+ windows, backing FR-03.

acceptance_criteria.given: recorded payments across Sep-2025 and Jul-2032
acceptance_criteria.when: the payment_ledger table is queried
acceptance_criteria.then: each payment appears as its own row with bond ref, month and paid flag, including months beyond Jul-2032

requirements.text: The system SHALL persist a Home Plan schedule entity (DATA-03) with month index 1..84, saving (including the irregular values 25000, 10000 and 0), rate, per-year interest, countdown, remaining interest and totals, backing FR-12.

acceptance_criteria.given: the imported home_plan rows
acceptance_criteria.when: months 1..84 are read
acceptance_criteria.then: each row carries its saving, rate, per-year interest, countdown and remaining interest, and the irregular savings 25000, 10000 and 0 are stored verbatim

acceptance_criteria.given: the schedule totals

## Derivation Rule

The RTM is COMPUTED from the store, not authored. The trace lanes are:

- `requirements.fr_id -> prd_items` — requirement trace (each SRS requirement back to its PRD statement)
- `prd_items.decision_id -> decisions` — decision trace (each PRD item back to its brainstorm decision D#)
- `acceptance_criteria -> test bindings` — test trace, added at Stage 8 (test_plan)

The `v_rtm` query/view regenerates the matrix from these links on demand; the table below is a carried-forward snapshot of the legacy mapping and is superseded by the computed view whenever the store changes.
